subject: Quality signal sync: A/B plan + pass/fail criteria for eval promptsets

Subject: Quality signal sync: A/B plan + pass/fail criteria for eval promptsets

Team —

We need to lock the acceptance criteria and A/B plan for the next eval run targeting the Llama-3 family variants. Goals: catch regressions in few-shot instruction-following and preserve retrieval-related answers. High-level asks: 

- Evelyn: can you confirm the pass/fail gates for the two promptset slices (instruction, retrieval) and list the primary metric(s)?
- Dev/Nikhil: what are the runtime / rollout constraints we should bake into the A/B (batch sizes, max latency SLOs, canary percentages)?
- Lauren: from CS/Customer POV, any hard no-fail criteria that would block release for customers on Dedicated?

Attached: eval_promptset_v2.json (prompt examples + scoring rubric) and an initial AB spec (ab_experiment_specs.xlsx). I want to run the first experiment week-of Oct 5; please reply with concrete numbers and objections by COB Sep 30 so we can finalize the launch checklist.

Thanks —
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Product — Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-09-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quality signal sync: A/B plan + pass/fail criteria for eval promptsets

+1 on timeline — quick notes from infra/runtime: 

- Canary sizing: we can do 5% traffic (min 250 qps-equivalent) or an opt-in 10% low-latency lane for Dedicated customers. For Hosted we should start at 1% and ramp to 5% over 48h.
- Latency SLOs: for the eval traffic we can tolerate median + P95 overhead up to +18% relative to baseline; anything above +25% flags automatic rollback.
- Batching: the experimental path will use dynamic batching with a max batch size of 32; if the A/B branch causes queuing beyond 120ms on average, we should cap concurrency or fall back immediately.

I added notes in rollout_fallback_notes.md. If Evelyn needs specific logging hooks for quality traces, call them out and we can add an extra trace header.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Engineering Manager, Serving Runtime
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-30T08:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quality signal sync: A/B plan + pass/fail criteria for eval promptsets

Thanks — I pulled the prompt slices into v2 and sketched pass/fail gates in the attached JSON. Summary of our acceptance criteria (short):

- Instruction slice (20k examples): Exact-match / helpfulness combined score must not drop more than 1.5 points on our 10-point scale vs. control. Any downward trend >2.0 triggers quarantine and root-cause eval.
- Retrieval slice (5k retrieval augmented examples): F1@tokens must stay within -3% of control; hallucination rate (false entity assertions per 1k tokens) must not increase by >0.5.
- Regression buckets: if any single benchmark task shows >4% degradation, fail gate.
- Statistical significance: require p < 0.05 and at least 300 paired samples for class-level assertions.

Operational checks we need from infra: per-request trace_id mapping to eval sample id and token-level loss dumps for failing samples. If you can wire those traces, I can produce a nightly triage summary during the experiment.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Lead Applied ML Scientist — Quality Evals
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-02T15:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quality signal sync: A/B plan + pass/fail criteria for eval promptsets

Operational constraints and rollout mechanics: 

- Deployment window: schedule the canary for off-peak for Hosted (03:00–06:00 UTC) to keep noise low. For Dedicated, we'll coordinate per-customer via CS.
- Canary ramp: 1% -> 5% over 48h -> 10% if stable (Hosted). Each step requires no pass/fail flags for 6h.
- Auto-fallback: on latency breach (>25% above baseline) or on Evelyn's fail gate, traffic should divert to the previous model variant and a page should be opened to #prod-ops.
- Observability: we need the eval job to emit sample-alignments and a live dashboard. I'll wire alerts for our two primary signals (instr delta, retrieval F1 delta).

Also — we should include a short runbook for escalation owners (CS, Engineering, Research) in case the gate trips. Draft attached.

-Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Principal SRE — Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-10-04T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quality signal sync: A/B plan + pass/fail criteria for eval promptsets

Quick customer perspective (I spoke with Acme Ops):

- Acme Ops is OK with a 5% Dedicated canary but wants an explicit ability to opt-out and a guarantee of zero change to retention/audit logs. They asked that any rollback include a short post-mortem and a credit if it impacted production queries.
- Suggested success thresholds they care about: end-user satisfaction delta <= 1 point (10-pt scale) and no increase in complaint rate > 0.3%.

If we incorporate these as contractual guardrails for Dedicated customers, we should add them to the experiment notes and the customer-facing KB. Happy to own coordination with Acme.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

2) If any rollback happens we want the post-mortem (1–2 page) within 3 business days and a brief note about what changed.

Looking forward to the run.
